summary: [SEV-3] Network Physical Layer Fault — veth0 @ DESKTOP-AVET5II

content.text: Automated network diagnostic report. Severity: SEV-3.

RCA: LAYER 1 PHYSICAL SIGNAL DEGRADATION — 15,509 RX CRC errors detected. CRC errors on fiber links typically indicate dirty or contaminated LC/UPC ferrules, exceeding fiber bend radius limits, or a marginal SFP+ transceiver.

OPTICAL POWER BUDGET EXCEEDED — Received optical power is -17.891 dBm, below the minimum acceptable threshold of -17.0 dBm. Possible causes: excessive fiber attenuation, dirty ferrules, bad fiber splice, or dying SFP+ laser diode.

remediation_steps: 🔬 STEP A — Inspect LC/UPC fiber connector ferrules with a fiber endface inspection scope (e.g. JDSU FBP-SD15 or Fluke FI-500 FiberInspector). Contaminated ferrules show as dark spots in the core region.

🧹 STEP B — Clean LC/UPC ferrules using a one-click fiber optic cleaner (e.g. Fujikura CLC-22). Clean both the patch cable and the SFP+ transceiver ferrule. NEVER blow with breath (moisture causes contamination).
📡 STEP C — After cleaning, re-measure optical RX power with `ethtool -m <iface>`. Target RX power range: -3.0 dBm to -13.0 dBm (current: -17.891 dBm).
🔭 STEP D — Use an optical power meter (e.g. EXFO PPM-350B) at the far end to measure insertion loss of the fiber run. Per-connector loss should be < 0.5 dB; total run loss < 3.5 dB for OM4 MMF.
🔁 STEP E — If optical loss is within budget, replace the SFP+ transceiver module. Use OEM-compatible modules meeting enterprise network specs (e.g. Finisar FTLX8571D3BCL for 10GBase-SR).
